test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Rohit marks the price of his article 60% more than its cost price. If he sells the article for ₹18,510 after allowing a discount of 85%, then what will be the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 60% of 100 = 160 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 160 × (100 − 85)% = 160 × 15% = 24 units.

Given, 24 units = 18,510.

1 unit = 18,510 ÷ 24 = 771.25.

100 units (CP) = 771.25 × 100 = 77,125.

**∴ The correct answer is 77,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 60%, Discount% = 85%, SP = 18,510.

**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/412ee95248e512959291ad32e0eb46a5208068dd2b3a6c1fffa521f74d797204.png] 

⇒ Let CP = x.

⇒ MP = x × (160 ÷ 100) = 1.6x.

⇒ SP = 1.6x × (15 ÷ 100) = 0.24x.

⇒ 0.24x = 18,510.

⇒ x = 18,510 ÷ 0.24 = 77,125.

**∴ The correct answer is 77,125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of CP to MP can be expressed using Profit% and Discount%: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Effective Gain/Loss

Net Change = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100. In this case: 60 − 85 − (60 × 85)/100 = −25 − 51 = −76% (Loss).</p
